  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale: The two live problems are measured declines in onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ), so the highest-leverage single slot is one that attacks the funnel stage that is actually degrading rather than one that buys volume at the top. memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging lifted week-one engagement) are the two inherited findings that speak directly to those declines, so those are the two I spend verification budget on: I want the original records' effect sizes, cohort definitions, and whether the lift was durable or a one-week novelty, because both are being applied 15-24 days after consolidation into a market that has since changed. I lean simplify_onboarding over activation_messaging because completion is the upstream gate — if accounts drop out before finishing onboarding, better activation messaging has a smaller addressable population — and because memory_86 is the more recent and broader-scoped of the two. I explicitly decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 says SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%, which is precisely the trade that fails the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; matching a price attack would buy a worse cohort. referral_incentive (memory_57) worked in established customers, not in the segment currently bleeding, and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses pipeline quality, not the SMB activation decline. Downstream value risk: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, and if verification shows memory_86's onboarding shortening also worked by removing data capture, then a completion lift can be purchased at the cost of firmographic and intent data that downstream qualification, routing, and personalization depend on — completion would rise while qualified revenue per account falls, and the harm would surface a quarter later than the win. So I will instrument this on qualified-pipeline and week-four retention, not just completion rate, and hold the data-capture fields that feed scoring. Uncertainty I am not collapsing: none of these memories carry confidence intervals, sample sizes, or segment breakouts in the inherited form; all predate the competitor's launch, so the price-sensitive segment composition may have shifted underneath them; and I cannot separate whether the activation decline is a funnel-mechanics problem or simply a worse-mix cohort arriving from a changed market. A standard_experiment with a proper holdout is the right scale — a small guarded test would not resolve a 4-6% effect against this noise, and a broad rollout would commit the whole funnel to a finding I have not yet re-verified.
